## When to start dialysis

There is no single kidney function threshold at which maintenance hemodialysis should begin. Nephrologists weigh symptoms, fluid and metabolic control, and patient preference alongside the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) [@hemmige2024density]. The IDEAL trial randomized adults with progressive chronic kidney disease to planned early or late starts and found no survival benefit from starting early [@cooper2010ideal]. After its publication in 2010, practice moved toward later initiation, which is why the cohort here begins in 2011.

## Why facility density

If eGFR alone does not dictate when dialysis starts, the surrounding health system may. The hypothesis of the paper is that areas organized around high-intensity treatment of end-stage disease, with many dialysis facilities per resident, start dialysis earlier than areas oriented toward prevention [@hemmige2024density]. Health Service Areas from the Dartmouth Atlas, groups of ZIP codes whose residents get most of their hospital care locally, serve as the unit for local practice patterns [@dartmouth_crosswalks].

## The measures

-   **eGFR at initiation** is calculated by the USRDS from the serum creatinine reported on the CMS-2728 Medical Evidence form, using the CKD-EPI equation [@levey2009ckdepi] with the race coefficient, because that is the value physicians saw when deciding.
-   **Facility density** counts the dialysis facilities listed by CMS in the patient's HSA on the date dialysis started, per 100,000 residents [@cms2025dfc].
-   **Area characteristics** come from the American Community Survey [@tidycensus], the USDA rural-urban commuting area codes [@ers2020ruca], and Dartmouth Atlas primary care and hospital measures [@dartmouth_primarycare; @dartmouth_capacity].
